actions.action: Check the soil moisture yourself instead of trusting the classifier label
Move the plant to the sunniest spot available
Rotate the plant so all sides get light
If very hot, put up shade cloth during the hottest hours
Alternatively, shelter the plant from afternoon sun reflecting off walls
Hand-pollinate by shaking or tapping the plant or using a small paintbrush, for a few weeks
Switch to a low-nitrogen, higher-potassium tomato/pepper fertilizer
Water deeply when the top inch of soil is dry to keep moisture even
Mulch the soil surface to keep roots cooler

reason: The plant was simply too immature to fruit and needed time, but the answer diagnoses blossom drop and prescribes several interventions instead of patience; those steps are unnecessary but unlikely to harm the plant.
